item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Mon Nov 9, 7:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: Women's and Men's Combined Breakfast (Assembly Room) — Sat Nov 14, 8:00 AM — Assembly Room
item.description:
At the Women’s Breakfast on Saturday, November 14, Tim Crist will discuss the research discoveries behind his book, New Englanders in a New Land, published by Rutgers University Press. In the book, Tim describes the way Congregationalists settled Newark in the 17th century and how they managed relationships with Native Americans and handled the question of slavery. Reviewers have commended Tim’s “impressive, pioneering research” and called the book “absorbing” in the way he “skillfully underscores the complexity of New Jersey’s origins by demonstrating how Newark’s leaders challenged the proprietary system in their quest to expand the New England model of godly authority and town self-government.” This program is open to everybody. Information about Tim’s book is available at: https://www.rutgersuniversitypress.org/new-englanders-in-a-new-land/9781978846883 Cover image: https://www.rutgersuniversitypress.org/media/catalog/product/9/7/9781978846906.jpg
Source: Union Congregational

item.title: Conestoga Trail and More Hike — Sun Nov 15, 8:30 AM
item.description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for this point to point hike, featuring the Conestoga Trail with great views, Wind Cave, Tucquan Glen, pleasant back roads, and back woods other trails. After meeting on the Enola Low Grade Trail lot, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to Pequea to begin our hike. We'll have a rougher first six miles on the Conestoga Trail with reroutes past House Rock and up into Tucquan Glen. We then follow pleasant back roads for a while, which are really nice for walking. This will be just under five miles. The final miles will mostly be within Martic Township Park, a large wooded tract. We'll meander though this until we reach the road near our end point and walk two tenths of a mile to the end. If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374
Source: Meetup: Metrotrails Hiking

item.title: Craft & Chat — Mon Nov 16, 1:00 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Bring your current project and join fellow makers for a relaxed afternoon of creativity and conversation. Whether you enjoy knitting, crocheting, embroidery, needlepoint, quilting, drawing, or other portable crafts, this is a welcoming space to work on your projects, share ideas, and connect with others who love to create.
There is no instructor and no formal program—just an opportunity to craft in the company of others. All skill levels are welcome. Please feel free to bring your own project and supplies, or explore the assortment of donated craft supplies available to use during the program. Supplies vary and are available while they last.
